intended_object: The specific real constant C = (∫_{ℝ³} (1+|ξ|²)^{-2} dξ)^{1/2}. It is the Cauchy–Schwarz constant used in the Fourier-side moment bound ∫|ξ||f̂| ≤ C·‖f‖_{H³}-type, which is how the same file uses it. Inferred from the docstring, the name and that use.
explanation:
The body is the square root of the Bochner integral of (1+‖ξ‖²)^{-2} over `Space`, which is `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)` with Lebesgue (volume) measure.

The integrand is integrable on ℝ³. It is about r^{-4} at infinity, and with the r² dr volume factor the radial integral converges. Its value is π², so C = π. The integral is therefore a genuine finite value, not Bochner's junk 0, and the definition matches the docstring's "finite numerical constant depending only on three-dimensional Lebesgue measure."

This is one specific number that the library uses in its three-dimensional Cauchy–Schwarz estimate (lines 67–109 of the same file). Being specific does not make it too narrow: its role is tied to dimension 3, and with the H³-weighted norm the exponent works out exactly there. Mathlib has no general counterpart to point to.
